headline: Vesugen
punch: What it claims, and what was actually measured.

headline: What it actually is
body: A synthetic tripeptide, **Lys-Glu-Asp**, from the Khavinson Peptide Institute. Its documented sequence is KED, which matters because the literature on this family is not always internally consistent about which peptide is which. | The claimed mechanism for the whole family is that these very short peptides enter the nucleus and bind DNA at specific promoter regions, modulating accessibility or methylation rather than acting as conventional receptor ligands.
punch: A three amino acid peptide said to act on DNA.

headline: The claim for growth
body: Vesugen's claimed effects are MSC proliferation, reduction in senescence markers, and progenitor recruitment via **CXCL12**. | If true, that would act on the growth plate's **resting-zone stem cell pool**, which is precisely the compartment whose exhaustion causes the plate to fuse. So the target is the right one. That is the strongest thing that can be said for it.
punch: It aims at the right compartment.

headline: Ashapkin 2020
body: This is the one study with actual numbers. KED and its relatives AED and KE were applied to human embryonic bone-marrow MSCs across two senescence models. | **IGF1 mRNA rose 3 to 5.6 fold.** In the passages model AED was +4.6x, KED +3x, KE +3.5x; in the stationary model AED +5.6x, KED +2x, KE +5.2x. A real, measured, several-fold rise in the growth factor people care about.
punch: IGF1 mRNA up 3 to 5.6 fold. Measured.

headline: Now the same study
body: In that identical experiment, **NFκB rose roughly 10 to 35 fold** in both models. That was the largest fold-change of any gene measured, several times larger than the IGF1 effect. | The authors' own interpretation is that this would be **expected to accelerate MSC aging**, since NFκB target genes are broadly pro-senescence and pro-inflammatory.

headline: And the rest flipped
body: TERT, the telomerase gene, was **suppressed** rather than raised. TNKS2 moved 4-fold down in one model and 6-fold up in the other, for the same peptide. FOXO1 changed sign between models too. | The authors attribute this to differing epigenetic context rather than a fixed direction of action. Which means the compound does not have a reliable effect, it has a context-dependent one.
punch: The same peptide, opposite directions, two models.

headline: The osteogenic problem
body: The source material claims Vesugen drives **osteogenic** but not **chondrogenic** differentiation. Those are different fates for the same stem cell. | Bone lengthening requires the resting-zone cell to become a chondrocyte and run the cartilage programme. Pushing a progenitor toward bone instead is not a slower version of that. It is a different outcome.
punch: Bone is not the lineage you want here.

headline: Dose has no basis
body: Every human dosing regimen across this family is a pulsed course of **10 to 30 days**, and the circulating dose figures are **not grounded in pharmacokinetic studies**. | There is a transporter rationale for intranasal delivery, since 2 to 4 residue peptides can use POT transporters which are expressed in human nasal epithelium. But **zero head-to-head injectable versus intranasal comparisons exist** for any of these compounds.
punch: No PK study. The dose is tradition.

headline: The mechanism is doubted
body: The claim that a three amino acid peptide binds DNA with sequence specificity is considered **biologically implausible by Western molecular biology standards**. Conventional transcription factors need DNA-binding domains of 30 to 60 or more residues to achieve that. | **No independent laboratory has replicated the core mechanism claims**, and the efficacy literature has not been replicated outside Russia.

headline: But it is probably safe
body: Being fair about the risk side, because the evidence problem and the safety problem are not the same problem. At 1 to 10 mg a day, these peptides are expected to be **hydrolysed into common dietary amino acids**. | On that basis the family is considered **low risk of harm** even by people who doubt the mechanism entirely. The realistic downside is cost and opportunity, not toxicity.

headline: Verdict
body: It targets the correct compartment and there is one real study showing a several-fold IGF1 rise. That same study shows a much larger NFκB rise the authors expect to accelerate ageing, suppressed telomerase, and genes that flip direction by model. | Zero evidence in a growing animal, no PK behind any dose, and a core mechanism no independent lab has reproduced. Low harm, low cost, and no reason to expect it to lengthen bone.
punch: Right target. Mixed signal. No growth data.
